nodes.question: Why is there uncertainty surrounding the deployment of Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR)?
nodes.answer: There is uncertainty because ambiguous amounts of residual emissions and the sectors they originate from complicate questions about which sectors or entities should be responsible for deploying or paying for CDR.
nodes.paragraph: REVIEWCurrent Sustainable/Renewable Energy Reports (2025) 12:6 https://doi.org/10.1007/s40518-25-252-1 Planting trees tends to be cheaper (ranging between $0 and $240 /t CO2 [3], as shown in Current Sustainable/Renewable Energy Reports (2025) 12:6 that stresses growing negative environmental effects when upscaling, particularly in the case of BECCS [ 12]. Second, Hollnaicher (2022) criticizes an overly high discount rate in the IAMs, which leads to an overestimation of CDR [ 13]. Third, the extent and originating sectors of so-called resid - ual emissions that are offset by CDR when countries reach net zero differ significantly in modeled scenario pathways [14 19]. Often residual emission estimates are not explic - itly defined in long-term national climate strategies, and for those countries that do define them, the level of residual emissions varies widely [ 16, 17]. Ambiguous amounts of residual emissions and the sectors in which these can take place lead to questions about responsible sectors or entities to deploy or pay for CDR [ 19]. Importantly, the emissions that are defined as residual come from notions of what is necessary and what is possible in the future, both of which are assumptions with political and justice implications [ 18].

nodes.question: What factors influence the economics of Direct Air Carbon Capture and Storage (DACCS)?
nodes.answer: The economics of DACCS varies depending on capture technology, energy costs, location, and whether the captured CO2 is stored or used.
nodes.paragraph: Recently, Climeworks has completed two commercial DACCS plants in Iceland (Orca, Mammoth) and aims to further upscale its technology in the United States (Project Cypress in Louisiana, Prairie Com - pass DAC Hub in North Dakota, and California DAC Hub in California). nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What technologies have been developed to address CO2 emissions?
nodes.answer: Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) technologies have been developed to tackle CO2 emissions.
nodes.paragraph: Although there are various efforts to enhance microalgae assimilation through genetic engineering or improvements of cultivation technologies (both closed Department of Chemical Technology, Faculty of Science, Chulalongkorn University, Pathumwan, Bangkok 10330, Thailand. 2Center of Excellence in Catalysis for Bioenergy and Renewable Chemicals (CBRC), Faculty of Science, Chulalongkorn University, Pathumwan, Bangkok 10330, Thailand. email: pichaya.i@chula.ac.th OPEN Scientific Reports www.nature.com/scientificreports and open systems), challenges persist, particularly concerning costs associated with downstream biorefinery processes5. Consequently, it is essential to investigate and develop additional technologies, integrating engineering knowledge with natural methods, to effectively handle the raising CO2 level. Over the past decades, Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) technologies have been developed to tackle CO2 emissions. Among them, an amine-based absorption is a prominent method for CO2 post- combustion capture from industrial flue gases and other point sources9. This technology demonstrates a high CO2 capture rate and efficiency compared to alternative methods (e.g. adsorption, membrane, and cryogenic processes)5,9. Furthermore, it can also be integrated with existing infrastructure, facilitating their adoption as a viable mitigation strategy in carbon management frameworks10.

nodes.question: How can post-combustion CO2 capture processes with phase-change solvents be assessed for environmental, health, and safety considerations?
nodes.answer: Post-combustion CO2 capture processes with phase-change solvents can be assessed for environmental, health, and safety considerations through a thorough assessment that evaluates the impact on the environment, potential health hazards, and overall safety aspects of the process.
